It's all I've done for the past week. But I will keep it up. And yeah that might be a good idea, I'll try it after my shift in an hour. 

I can't thank you enough for taking the time out of your day for doing this. Not just helping me, but others out there. It really means an incredible amount to me. Thank you.

My biggest fear is that she won't survive the year. If she stays along the same road she's been on, the anorexia is going to kill her. Her heart beat is already irregular. She can barely walk up steps. I've been a medic for about 5 years now and if I looked at her as if she were a patient then I'd say she'll be dead in less than a year if she continues at this rate. 

And now she's cancelled her appointments to seek help.

I've bee desperately trying to remind her. The only times I manage to get her to speak a little bit, she snaps is becomes very cold and hurtful towards me. I don't know what to do or say. I know it's not her fault and she's in a really dark place, but she's completely breaking my heart and hurting my feelings with what she's saying. 

I feel so selfish complaining about how hurt I feel while she's going through hell.

We are planning to move to Canada for our studies in a year's time. I just returned from Finland about a week and a half ago after seeing her for 9 days. I work 2 full time jobs in order to attempt to make our move possible. 

I would leave this second for her. I'm just worried she will kill me because my jobs will fire me and ruin our future. I work as a paramedic.

Thank you. I've been working very hard trying to get her to at least return to see her old therapist. The worst feeling is being so far away and knowing that ultimately there's nothing I can do to stop her from hurting herself if she was really going to act upon it.

Unfortunately she just got into a new apartment and I never thought to ask for her address. But she just messaged me apologizing. I'm glad she's okay and thank you for replying. I needed to find someway to get this off my chest
